text: Non-human identities, including the LLM ordering assistant, are verified and authorized on every request like human identities
Authenticate every request to the order portal, stock and contract services against the corporate identity provider
Evaluate the access policy per request using role, device, context and data domain (order, stock, contract)
Require step-up multi-factor authentication for privileged actions such as contract price changes, credit limit changes and release of quarantined stock
Cache policy decisions for non-privileged read requests for a short period while always re-verifying privileged actions
Issue a dedicated service identity to the LLM ordering assistant and restrict each assistant request to the entitlements of the authenticated end user on whose behalf it acts
Verify the identity of the requester before releasing order, contract or personal data to a hospital buyer or an external party
Perform a quarterly review and recertification of all user and service account entitlements and record the outcome
Log every access decision (allow or deny) with the identity, data domain and timestamp, and use the log as evidence for the quarterly review
Identity provider (single source of user and service identities for the portal, back office and assistant)
Policy decision point
Multi-factor and step-up authentication service
Access review register recording entitlements, reviewers and decisions per quarter
Order portal and order management module as the protected systems holding order, stock and contract data
IT Security Officer (owner of access policy, identity provider and the verification controls)
Sales Administrator (internal user of order and contract data, subject to per-request verification)
Hospital Buyer (external portal user whose requests are authenticated and authorized individually)
Responsible Pharmacist (approver of privileged pharmaceutical actions requiring step-up authentication)
Data Protection Officer (verifies that identity checks and data access rules protect personal data)
Quality Assurance Officer (reviewer of access rights to regulated order and batch-related data in the quarterly review)
AI Product Owner (accountable for the LLM assistant's service identity and its scoped entitlements)
No network location, including the office network, is trusted by default
The LLM ordering assistant holds no entitlements of its own; it only acts within the rights of the authenticated user it serves
Regulation requires traceable records of who accessed and changed regulated order, batch and contract data
Shared accounts are not permitted for users, administrators or the LLM assistant
Identity is verified before any order, contract or personal data is released
Only the Responsible Pharmacist may authorize release of quarantined medicines, and only after step-up multi-factor authentication
A confirmed order cannot be edited without a change request, and such edits are treated as privileged actions
